title: Create Your Own Token
objectives: Learn what mint authority and freeze authority mean
Discover why anyone can launch a token on a permissionless blockchain
Understand the security implications of revoking mint authority

steps.title: Anyone Can Mint a Token
steps.body:
Blockchains are permissionless: you do not need permission from a government, bank, or corporation to invent a new token. There is no application form and no gatekeeper - just code.

To create a token, you instruct the Solana Token Program to initialize a new <Term id="mint">Mint account</Term>. You choose the name, ticker symbol, decimals, and initial <Term id="total_supply">total supply</Term>.

**The flip side of freedom.** The exact same 30-second process is available to scammers, meme-coin factories, and rug-pull artists. Nobody audits a token before it goes live; nobody approves it. That means the burden of checking a token's settings falls entirely on *you*, the buyer. Permissionlessness is why crypto is open - and why you must learn to read what a token is really allowed to do.

steps.title: Mint Authority: The Printing Press
steps.body:
When a token is created, an address is assigned as the **Mint Authority** - think of it as the printing press.

**What it can do:** whoever controls that address can print brand-new tokens at any time, at zero cost. Each new token dilutes every existing holder and can be dumped on the market, crashing the price. An active mint authority is one of the most common <Term id="rug_pull">rug pull</Term> risks in new launches.

**The honest move - revoke it.** In trustworthy projects, the creator permanently **revokes** (sets to `null`) the mint authority right after launch. This is a cryptographic promise: because the Token Program code cannot be changed, the maximum supply is now frozen forever. No one - not even the original developer - can ever print another token.

So when you inspect a token, the first question is simple: **is mint authority revoked?** If not, you are trusting a stranger not to print money out of thin air.

steps.title: Under the Hood: Mint Authority in Account State
steps.body: A Solana mint account holds a 82-byte data structure containing: `mint_authority` (Option<Pubkey>), `supply` (u64), `decimals` (u8), `is_initialized` (bool), and `freeze_authority` (Option<Pubkey>). When authority is revoked, the `COption::None` tag is written to memory. Because the Token Program code cannot be modified, no one, not even the original creator, can ever print another token.

questions.prompt: What does 'Revoking Mint Authority' do for a token?
options: Destroys all existing tokens in holders' wallets
Permanently fixes the maximum supply so no new tokens can ever be printed
Changes the token name to Bitcoin
questions.explainRight: Correct! Revoking mint authority proves to investors that the creators cannot inflate or print more tokens.
questions.explainWrong: Incorrect. Revoking mint authority locks the supply so nobody can ever print new tokens in the future.

questions.prompt: If a memecoin creator keeps the mint authority active, what risk do buyers face?
options: The creator could mint billions of free tokens for themselves and dump them on the market
questions.explainRight: Spot on! An un-revoked mint authority is a common rug-pull risk in newly launched tokens.
questions.explainWrong: Incorrect. An active mint authority allows the creator to print unlimited tokens and crash the price.
